preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 200000 for n in [int(stdin.split()[0])]) and all(1 <= k <= n for k in [int(stdin.split()[1])])
preconditions.description: Input contains valid integers n (number of nodes) and k (number of nodes inspected), where 2 ≤ n ≤ 200,000 and 1 ≤ k ≤ n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(a) <= 1000000 for a in stdin.split()[2:2+n])
preconditions.description: The list of n integers a_i (time spent on each node) satisfies 1 ≤ a_i ≤ 1,000,000.

preconditions.expression: len([line for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:] if line.strip()]) == n - 1
preconditions.description: The input contains exactly n-1 edges representing a tree structure (connected, acyclic, undirected).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(v) <= n and int(u) != int(v) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:] for u, v in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes u_i and v_i within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.description: Output is a single integer representing the maximum possible grade Jacob can achieve by optimally choosing the root and ordering neighbors.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == max(min(a_i for a_i in dfs_first_k(root, k, tree, a)) for root in range(1, n+1) for ordering in neighbor_orderings(tree, root))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum of the minimum a_i values in the first k nodes of any DFS traversal starting from any root and any neighbor ordering. Here, `dfs_first_k(root, k, tree, a)` returns the first k a_i values in DFS order starting at `root`, and `neighbor_orderings(tree, root)` generates all possible neighbor orderings for the tree rooted at `root`.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= 1000000 for a_i in [int(a) for a in stdin.split()[2:2+n]])
postconditions.description: The output is derived from the given a_i values, ensuring no invalid or out-of-bounds values are considered.
